page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this server provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, though it lacks AMX capabilities. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute workloads. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1576.19 and a multi-core score of 8311.36, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 4693.0. However, memory performance exhibits a notable bottleneck; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 465.3 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth falls into the bottom 25% at 37.76 GB/sec. Similarly, the Passmark memory score and database operations benchmarks are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is highly constrained, with the medium 7B model achieving poor text generation speeds of 5.5 tokens per second.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers a memory-dense hardware profile without the added cost of bundled local storage or integrated GPUs. It is suited for workloads requiring moderate compute coupled with high memory capacity, such as in-memory caching, Redis deployments (achieving 8.03 million operations per second in testing), and static web serving. It is less suitable for memory-bandwidth-intensive database operations or large-scale machine learning inference due to the documented performance drops in large-block memory reads and medium-model LLM execution.
